feed.title: OOZEMeter — Oozeonomics
feed.subtitle: The study of economic slime. One score for U.S. economic stress, from public data.

entry.title: The Ooze Report: the household number held, and the market calmed down
entry.summary: June is still the last sealed month, so the household score didn't move. Ward M fell ten points as the semiconductor selloff reversed and market weakness stopped spreading.

entry.title: Ooze Level June 2026: 26/100 (Sticky)
entry.summary: The June 2026 Ooze Level sealed at 26 out of 100 — Sticky territory, down 3 from May 2026. Calmer than 6 of every 10 months since 2003. The heaviest line was housing at 6 ounces. The relief came from the two lines everyone feels first: gas prices (down 11 points) and inflation (down 9 points). Every figure is computed from cited public data and passed the facility's integrity gate before publication.

entry.title: The Ooze Report: June reads 26, and the expensive things didn't move
entry.summary: Gas prices eased and inflation cooled, so households got a little breathing room in June. Housing, credit cards and car payments did not budge.

entry.title: Correction: the archive printed ounces that did not sum to the reading
entry.summary: For roughly two hours on 2 August 2026, all eleven household archive reconstructions printed contribution figures on the wrong scale. The parts exceeded the whole by 7 to 11 ounces. Here is what happened and what changed in the machine.

entry.title: Gas prices: the number America reads twice a week
entry.summary: Posted in foot-tall numbers on every corner, paid on a schedule nobody chooses — why the pump is the economy's mood ring, and how the facility meters it.

entry.title: Housing: the biggest bill and the biggest asset, at the same time
entry.summary: Most families' largest monthly payment is also their largest store of wealth. When mortgage rates climb, the whole chain slows — and history says this line deserves its thick pipe.

entry.title: Credit cards: the economy's smoke detector
entry.summary: Cards are the first bill households skip when budgets crack. Rising delinquency means kitchen-table budgets are failing months before any headline says so.

entry.title: Auto loans: the most defended payment in the budget
entry.summary: In most of America, no car means no job. When auto delinquencies rise, the stress has already burned through every other line of defense.

entry.title: Unemployment: the heaviest line in the jar
entry.summary: Every other pressure is survivable with a paycheck. This is the line that turns a squeeze into a crisis — and why it carries the formula's largest weight.

entry.title: Inflation: the pressure that makes every other line heavier
entry.summary: Inflation is not one price rising — it is the ruler shrinking. How the facility meters purchasing power, and why deflation once kept a declaration off the board.

entry.title: Financial Conditions: the plumbing gauge — and the bet behind it
entry.summary: The jar's seventh line reads the financial system's plumbing through 105 indicators. It entered at 3% as a labeled bet, and this is the full disclosure.

entry.title: The foreclosure line: why the cascade's terminal stage reads AUX
entry.summary: Every filing is a family that ran out of every option. So why does this line carry zero weight? A case study in honest proxies.

entry.title: The manufacturing sensor: the factory floor as early warning
entry.summary: Factories feel slowdowns before households do — orders vanish before paychecks. Why this classic signal rides at zero weight, on public data only.

entry.title: How the Ooze Score works: the whole recipe in plain English
entry.summary: Seven lines, fixed weights, published anchors, one calibration rule — and a robot that collects it daily. No black boxes, by construction.

entry.title: SMOOTH to OVERFLOWING: what each band of the meter feels like
entry.summary: A number needs a scale that means something. The five bands, what each feels like at the kitchen table, and the ☢ condition that has never been met.

entry.title: Ward M: why markets got their own jar instead of a seat in ours
entry.summary: The boss wanted the stock market in the score. The studies said no — and yes. The full story of the facility's market wing, and the divergence it exists to show.

entry.title: What is Oozeonomics?
entry.summary: The study of economic slime: how stress actually moves through household budgets, measured instead of narrated.

entry.title: 2008 missed OOZEMAXING by exactly one line
entry.summary: The backtest found something nobody knew: even the Great Financial Crisis never tripped the everything-fails-at-once alarm.

entry.title: The vibecession, measured: why 2022 only scored 24
entry.summary: Everyone hated that economy. The cascade data says households mostly held. Both things are true.

entry.title: June seals at 26: the jar drains 3 points
entry.summary: Gas and inflation eased at the same time — the biggest one-month relief since the winter.
